_README: HIDDEN UNBLINDING KEY for the RQ2 rating form. This file maps each item to the condition behind its A and B labels. It is not needed to run the form and must never be linked from it, pasted into it, or sent to a rater — it is read only after responses are collected, by eval/rq2_analysis.py. `form_item_number` is the item's position in the form, which is how a response CSV joins back to it: the per-item questions are worded identically across items, so the columns are told apart by order, not by name.
form_title: Comparing Two Tutoring Response Styles (10 items, ~10 min)
length_ratio_note: Response length is NOT matched between conditions. The measured ratio for this frozen set is 1.31x (51.7 vs 39.6 mean words); report that number rather than describing the conditions as length-matched.

post_freeze_edits.change: Removed two simulator scripting quote marks that butted two scripted speech segments together (`... somewhere else?" "Is that right?` -> `... somewhere else? Is that right?`). The marks were the simulator's, not the student's, and would have been visible to raters.
post_freeze_edits.note: Hand-edit, not a regeneration. Both coach responses for this pair are byte-identical to the generated ones: the scaffolded anchor is drawn from earlier in the utterance and the answer-giving condition never reads student text. No other pair was touched. This file is therefore the generated set plus this one recorded text edit, not a verbatim pipeline output.

questions.which_helps: Which response would actually help you understand how to solve this, not just get the answer?
questions.rate_a: Rate Response A — how helpful is this for actually learning the concept?
questions.rate_b: Rate Response B — how helpful is this for actually learning the concept?
questions.when_stuck: If you were stuck and stressed, which response would you rather receive right now?
questions.free_text: Anything either response got wrong, confusing, or annoying?
questions.overall: Across all the items you just saw, which style did you generally prefer?
questions.grade: What grade or year are you in?
questions.math_relationship: How would you describe your relationship with math?
